newsitem.title: UK: UK's Lang pledges easier retail rules.
newsitem.headline: UK's Lang pledges easier retail rules.

text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang on Tuesday promised British retailers that if reelected in the May 1 election the Conservative Party would ease regulations in the sector.
At the same time, he warned a retail indusrty conference that a Labour government would be a "gamble which industry should think twice about before taking".
Lang said Labour's plan to introduce a national minimum wage and less flexible working hours would damage the industry.
"The introduction of a minimum wage will hurt most those whom it tries to help," Lang said.

Lang, speaking one day after Prime Minister John Major set the election date, said the Conservatives would introduce a "sunset clause" into new regulations so that regulations would automatically expire in time unless they were specifically renewed.
He also pledged to raise the audit exemption level for smaller retailers from 90,000 pounds to 350,000 pounds thus freeing 200,000 small businesses from the annual requirement to submit accounts.
